body.box_text: For the latest data about the cost of living and food read our bulletins on;

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Prices of food and non-alcoholic beverages rose by 7.0% in the year to January 2024 according to the latest [Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2024).

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: This was the tenth consecutive month of falls in food inflation, down from 8.0% in December and a recent high of 19.2% in March 2023, which was the highest annual rate seen for over 45 years.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: The latest food and non-alcoholic beverage inflation rate is the lowest since April 2022.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: The easing in the inflation rate was driven by prices for bread and cereals, which fell 1.3% on the month. This was the largest fall in bread and cereals prices since May 2021.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Although the rate at which food prices are rising has slowed, they remain high.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: The overall price of food and non-alcoholic beverages rose around 25% between January 2022 and January 2024. In the 10 years prior to this, overall food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose by 9%.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Prices in restaurants and cafes rose by 8.2% in the year to January 2024, up from 7.7% in the year to December 2023.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: As prices remain high compared with recent years, 40% of adults in Great Britain say they have spent more than usual to get what they normally buy when food shopping within the past two weeks.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: This was according to those asked between 17 and 28 January 2024 as part of our latest [Public opinions and social trends bulletin](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain17to28january2024).

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: The latest survey also reveals that more than 4 in 10 (44%) adults said they were buying less food when shopping in the last two weeks.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Rising food costs was the most commonly reported reason among the 49% of adults who said their cost of living had risen compared with a month ago.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Of those, 91% said one of the reasons for their rising costs was higher food shopping prices.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: Meanwhile, around 1 in 25 adults (4%) have reported that their household had run out of food and could not afford to buy more in the past two weeks, according to [more detailed analysis from the survey covering the period 18 October, 2023 to 1 January 2024](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/theimpactofwinterpressuresondifferentpopulationgroupsingreatbritain18october2023to1january2024).

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: This is similar to late autumn and winter 2022.

body.h4: Food price inflation falls to lowest level since April 2022
body.text: You can explore how the prices of 450 items in the inflation basket – including the cost of food and eating out - have increased over the past year with our [shopping prices comparison tool](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/shoppingpricescomparisontool/2023-05-03).
